data.title: Wallet Provisioning Following OTP Interception Indicator
data.description: Detects digital wallet provisioning events where the OTP or verification code was delivered within minutes of a social engineering indicator, such as an inbound call from a suspicious source, a phishing link click, or a smishing response. Legitimate wallet provisioning is typically self-initiated, with OTP-to-provisioning intervals of 30-120 seconds. When provisioning occurs within 15 seconds of OTP delivery, or when OTP delivery is preceded by a phishing or social engineering indicator within a 30-minute window, this strongly suggests automated interception-to-provision attack chains associated with digital wallet fraud (TP-0037). The card provisioning attempt is the critical disruption point where refined controls can prevent downstream contactless fraud.

enrichment_required.source: Device profiling enrichment (first-seen timestamp from device intelligence)

falsepositives: Legitimate cardholders who provision wallets very quickly after receiving OTP
Tech-savvy users with automated provisioning workflows on trusted devices
Corporate card administrators provisioning multiple devices in rapid succession
